human_actions_pending.action: Decide the PR shape for branch gsd/debug-windows-publish-one-asset.
human_actions_pending.context: It holds 24a2597 (the 471-line root-cause report), is 1 commit ahead of origin/main, UNPUSHED, with no PR. Quick 260726-4cc is deliberately committing to this SAME branch (branch_name resolved null), so the natural shape is ONE PR covering the root-cause report plus the four fixes it motivated -- reviewed together. decisions.decision: All four proposals APPLY. Nothing dropped.
decisions.rationale: Research returned HIGH confidence on each. The triage was real -- Proposal 2 had a pre-committed DROP condition it had to survive, and it did.

decisions.decision: Proposal 2's dedup is safe and the all-miss gate needs NO adjustment.
decisions.rationale: Q1 proof: actionsCache.get(hash) derives both arguments from `hash` alone and `version` is discarded by listCacheEntries before the engine sees it, so every row sharing a key returns an identical outcome. readMisses increments 0 or m_h times for a hash, never partially, so readMisses and hashes.length are weighted sums over the SAME multiplicity vector and multiplicity cancels. Today's gate already means 'every DISTINCT hash missed'. The dangerous direction (dedup makes the gate miss a genuine total regression) was hunted and proven impossible.
P2 redefines hashes.length from enumerated (key,version) ROWS to DISTINCT hashes, so `scanned` must exist and be tested before its denominator moves. Confirmed load-bearing by research.

decisions.decision: `readMisses` is presented as a SUBSET of `skipped`, never a sibling row.
decisions.rationale: publish-mirror.ts:185-186 increments BOTH. Sibling rows would make every reader double-count. Research called this the single design decision Proposal 1 most needs to get right; the label itself carries the relation.

decisions.decision: The all-miss gate predicate stays BYTE-IDENTICAL.
decisions.rationale: It is the only automated detector for a regressed Actions-cache read scope -- the failure mode the debug investigation proved is otherwise invisible. Research proved equivalence under dedup, so any edit is unjustified risk.

decisions.decision: One atomic commit per proposal; the full 8-command battery green at EVERY commit.
decisions.rationale: Explicit user instruction (bisect-safe, atomic). Not just green at the end.
branch_name resolved null (quick_branch_template is an ignored unknown config key), and the debug report plus the fixes it motivated belong in one reviewable unit.

decisions.decision: Out of scope: anything making a publish leg mirror another OS's entries; and U2.
decisions.rationale: The debug file explicitly does not recommend cross-OS mirroring (enableCrossOsArchive would change every derived version and invalidate the whole existing mirror). U2 (nx-cache-cafe<runid> entries existing only in a Linux version) is a distinct thread.

context_notes: The plan is execute-ready and independently checked -- resume by executing, not by re-planning or re-triaging. Three numeric traps will bite an executor who skims: (1) do NOT hardcode scanned = 37 anywhere, because after Task 2 the same measured run scans 25 DISTINCT hashes rather than 37 rows, and a 37 assertion would break AT the Task 2 commit and destroy the bisect-safety the user asked for; (2) the debug file's E4 mirrored/skipped pairs (ubuntu 6/32, windows 2/24) do NOT close arithmetically because `skipped` INCLUDES `readMisses` -- the trustworthy figures are the ROW counts only: 37 rows per leg, ubuntu 36 hit + 1 miss, windows 25 hit + 12 miss, 25 distinct keys, 12 dual-version; (3) CONTEXT.md's illustrative summary line has the same defect and is superseded. On the bundle: check:action regenerates start-cache-server/index.js, and publish-mirror.ts is NOT reachable from the bundle entry (entry.ts imports serve() only), so no drift is expected -- but if check:action ever fails, stage the regenerated bundle in the SAME commit, because a drifted bundle in its own commit breaks bisect. Why Task 1 matters at all: the debug investigation's entire cost came from three compounding blind spots that made a benign 4/1 asset split indistinguishable from a regressed read scope -- @actions/cache logs restore MISSes at core.debug (cache.js:294), the summary had no scanned row and folded misses into skipped, and the all-miss warning only fires on a TOTAL miss. Task 1 closes the second of those three.
